q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT DISTINCT P.EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON AS P LEFT JOIN PERSON AS DP ON P.EMAIL = DP.EMAIL WHERE P.ID <> DP.ID

explanation: Q1 groups the records by email and checks if the count of emails is greater than 1, which will return all emails that appear more than once in the table. Q2, on the other hand, uses a self-join to find distinct emails that have at least one duplicate in the table.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least one email that appears more than once in the table, and another email that appears only once. The email that appears more than once should have at least one duplicate in the table.
